name: Aquarium Plants (Freshwater and Marine)
description: Common freshwater aquarium plants plus macroalgae, seagrasses and mangroves for marine tanks, with placement, growth, height, light, CO2 and water parameters.

fieldDefinitions.heightCm: Average height in the aquarium (Tropica: after two months); null for floating plants and algae
fieldDefinitions.herbivoreResistant: true = usually left alone by herbivorous fish
fieldDefinitions.verifiedFields: Fields individually checked against the cited source; other values are guide values based on nursery data and standard literature
fieldDefinitions.legal.euInvasiveList: true = on the EU Union list (trade and keeping ban)

notes: Plant values are guide values; growth and height depend strongly on light, CO2 and fertilisation.
Never dispose of aquarium plants, plant material or aquarium water into natural waters or garden ponds.
Marine tanks mostly keep macroalgae; many of them are used for nutrient export in the refugium.

plantEatingSpecies.description: Species from the species lists that eat or uproot plants. Plants with herbivoreResistant = true or epiphytes on wood and stone are suitable for them.

plants.name: Dwarf Anubias
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Small, very hardy rhizome plant that grows under almost all conditions and, according to Tropica, is not eaten by herbivorous fish.
plants.careNotes: Slow growth: leaves live for years and slow-growing algae easily settle on them. Do not bury the rhizome, otherwise it rots.

plants.name: Anubias barteri
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Larger Anubias with heart-shaped, leathery leaves; ideal for tanks with herbivorous or digging fish.
plants.careNotes: Tie to roots; tolerates shade. Like all Anubias prone to algae on old leaves.

plants.name: Java Fern
plants.propagation: Plantlets on the leaves, rhizome division
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Classic, almost indestructible water fern that most herbivores avoid. Forms plantlets directly on the leaves.
plants.careNotes: Attach to wood or stone. Optimal at 22–28 °C according to Dennerle.

plants.name: African Water Fern
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Dark green, finely structured fern from flowing waters; creates strong accents on roots.
plants.careNotes: Grows without CO2; CO2 and soft, slightly acidic water significantly accelerate growth. Likes current.

plants.name: Bucephalandra
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Small, leathery epiphytes from fast-flowing streams of Borneo in many colour forms; popular for details on stones and roots.
plants.careNotes: Very slow growth; keep the rhizome free.

plants.name: Java Moss
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Undemanding moss that clings to any surface; grazing area and hiding place for shrimp and fry.
plants.careNotes: Thin out regularly so the inside does not rot; also tolerates cooler water.

plants.name: Christmas Moss
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Moss with shoots branching like fir trees; grows more regularly than Java moss.
plants.careNotes: Somewhat more light promotes the typical growth form.

plants.name: Phoenix Moss
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Very small, fan-shaped moss for details on stones and wood.
plants.careNotes: Grows very slowly but compactly.

plants.name: Pellia
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Liverwort with flat, forked thalli; forms cushion-like patches.
plants.careNotes: Attaches less well than mosses – fix with a net or glue.

plants.name: Crystalwort (Riccia)
plants.substrate: Floating or attached to stones with a net
plants.description: Floating liverwort that forms green cushions with oxygen pearls when fixed under nets.
plants.careNotes: Stays compact when attached only with good light and CO2; must be re-tied regularly.

plants.name: Wendt's Water Trumpet
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Very variable, hardy Cryptocoryne in green to brown forms; Dennerle states 20–28 °C, pH 5–8 and very soft to hard water.
plants.careNotes: Typical is 'crypt melt' (leaves dissolve after replanting or changes in water parameters); the plant regrows from the rootstock. Avoid replanting if possible.

plants.name: Cryptocoryne parva
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Smallest Cryptocoryne; according to Tropica needs more light than most Cryptocorynes and must not be shaded.
plants.careNotes: Plant individual plants a few centimetres apart; after about six months a closed, low group forms.

plants.name: Beckett's Water Trumpet
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Hardy Cryptocoryne with olive-green to brownish leaves.
plants.careNotes: Like all Cryptocorynes sensitive to sudden changes in water parameters.

plants.name: Wavy Water Trumpet
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Cryptocoryne with narrow, wavy leaves.
plants.careNotes: Forms dense groups via runners.

plants.name: Cryptocoryne balansae
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Tall Cryptocoryne with long, strongly wavy, ribbon-like leaves for the background.
plants.careNotes: Tolerates moderately hard to hard water well.

plants.name: Amazon Sword
plants.propagation: Adventitious plantlets on the flower stalk
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Classic large sword plant with broad, light green leaves; dominant solitary plant in large tanks.
plants.careNotes: Heavy root feeder – regularly place root tabs near the roots. Grows too large for small tanks.

plants.name: Echinodorus 'Ozelot'
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Cultivar with red-brown spotted leaves; hardy eye-catcher in the midground.
plants.careNotes: Root fertilisation enhances the spotting.

plants.name: Dwarf Chain Sword
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Small, grass-like plant that forms a lawn via runners.
plants.careNotes: Flat and dense in good light, otherwise taller and looser.

plants.name: Dwarf Sagittaria
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Hardy, grass-like plant that spreads quickly via runners.
plants.careNotes: Low lawn in strong light, considerably taller in low light.

plants.name: Tiger Vallisneria
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Striped Vallisneria for beginners that, according to Tropica, grows in virtually all light and water conditions; leaves 30–50 cm long.
plants.careNotes: Forms runners easily. Also grows well in hard water.

plants.name: Giant Vallisneria
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Very large Vallisneria with leaves up to a metre long that float at the surface and provide shade.
plants.careNotes: Only for tall tanks; do not trim leaves but remove them completely.

plants.name: Aponogeton crispus
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Tuberous plant with wavy, translucent leaves; often flowers in the aquarium.
plants.careNotes: May enter dormancy periods during which it loses leaves.

plants.name: Tiger Lotus
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Water lily with green or red spotted underwater leaves; eye-catcher in the midground.
plants.careNotes: Remove floating leaves if compact underwater growth is wanted; otherwise they shade the tank.

plants.name: African Onion Plant
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Bulb plant with very long, narrow, strongly crinkled leaves; tough and usually left alone by herbivores.
plants.careNotes: Bury the bulb only halfway.

plants.name: Dwarf Hairgrass 'Mini'
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Lower form of hairgrass; according to Tropica one of the most reliable species for a dense lawn with little maintenance.
plants.careNotes: Plant in small portions; needs good light for optimal growth.

plants.name: Dwarf Hairgrass
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Fine, grass-like plant; flat lawn or taller tufts depending on light.
plants.careNotes: Trim regularly for a dense lawn.

plants.name: Brazilian Micro Sword
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Low plant with spatula-shaped leaves that slowly forms a dense lawn.
plants.careNotes: Needs patience; CO2 speeds up spreading.

plants.name: Water Clover
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Undemanding carpeting plant; underwater usually only with single, clover-like leaves.
plants.careNotes: Also grows without CO2, but slowly.

plants.name: Glossostigma
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: One of the smallest aquarium plants; according to Tropica difficult, with high light and CO2 demand.
plants.careNotes: Grows upwards with too little light. CO2 and soft water significantly promote growth.

plants.name: Dwarf Baby Tears (HC 'Cuba')
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: One of the smallest aquarium plants with millimetre-sized leaves; according to Tropica not difficult, but needs plenty of light, CO2, flow and fertiliser.
plants.careNotes: Trim the carpet regularly, otherwise the lower parts die. Tropica recommends 'Monte Carlo' as a less demanding alternative.

plants.name: Monte Carlo
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Light green carpeting plant with roundish leaves; less demanding than Dwarf Baby Tears.
plants.careNotes: Also grows in partial shade, but becomes considerably more compact with good light and CO2.

plants.name: Staurogyne repens
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Compact, bushy foreground plant from the Rio Cristalino; forms creeping side shoots.
plants.careNotes: Shorten the longest upright shoots when planting; grows more upright in low light.

plants.name: Downoi
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Small plant with star-shaped, wavy leaves; unusual texture for the foreground.
plants.careNotes: Prefers rather warm water; yellow leaves with nutrient deficiency.

plants.name: Hydrocotyle tripartita
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Creeping plant with small, three-lobed leaves; grows between stones and over wood.
plants.careNotes: Grows fast and must be trimmed regularly.

legal.note: Do not confuse with floating pennywort (Hydrocotyle ranunculoides), which is on the EU Union list.

plants.name: Rotala rotundifolia
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: According to Tropica undemanding, unlike other Rotala species; but needs good light for red leaves.
plants.careNotes: Branches strongly; trim often so the lower leaves get light.

plants.name: Rotala wallichii
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Finely feathered, reddish stem plant; needs soft water, plenty of light and CO2.
plants.careNotes: Sensitive to iron and nutrient deficiency.

plants.name: Creeping Primrose-willow (Ludwigia repens)
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Hardy stem plant with green-red to deep red leaves.
plants.careNotes: More light and iron intensify the red colouration.

legal.note: Do not confuse with Ludwigia grandiflora and L. peploides (both on the EU Union list).

plants.name: Ludwigia 'Super Red'
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Intensely red cultivar for colour accents.
plants.careNotes: Full red colour only with good light and nutrient supply.

plants.name: Alternanthera reineckii 'Mini'
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Compact, slower-growing miniature form; can be trimmed into a red-violet cushion of 5–10 cm.
plants.careNotes: Plenty of light and CO2 improve growth and colour.

plants.name: Alternanthera reineckii
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Red to pink stem plant for colour contrasts.
plants.careNotes: With insufficient light the lower leaves lose their colour and drop off.

plants.name: Dwarf Ambulia
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Finely feathered, fast-growing stem plant; good nutrient competitor against algae.
plants.careNotes: Forms dense stands in strong light; trim shoots regularly.

plants.name: Giant Hygrophila
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Hardy, large-leaved stem plant for the background.
plants.careNotes: Grows fast and removes many nutrients from the water.

plants.name: Water Wisteria
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Plant with strongly feathered leaves; beginner plant.
plants.careNotes: Holes in the leaves indicate potassium deficiency.

plants.name: Dwarf Hygrophila
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: One of the most undemanding aquarium plants with very fast growth.
plants.careNotes: Grows so fast that it can overgrow slower plants.

legal.note: Not on the EU Union list, but classified as invasive in the USA (Federal Noxious Weed). Never let plant material get into natural waters.

plants.name: Lemon Bacopa
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Hardy plant with thick, slightly fragrant leaves.
plants.careNotes: Copper-coloured shoot tips in strong light.

plants.name: Moneywort (Bacopa monnieri)
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Small-leaved, very hardy stem plant.
plants.careNotes: Tolerates hard water well.

plants.name: Stargrass
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Narrow-leaved stem plant that grows creeping or upright.
plants.careNotes: Creeping, bushy growth in strong light.

plants.name: Green Milfoil
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Finely feathered, light green stem plant.
plants.careNotes: Fine leaves easily collect debris – good flow and filtration.

legal.note: Do not confuse with Myriophyllum aquaticum and M. heterophyllum (both on the EU Union list).

plants.name: Ammannia gracilis
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Sturdy stem plant with orange-red, narrow leaves.
plants.careNotes: Colour and growth depend strongly on light and nutrients.

plants.name: Pearlweed
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Small-leaved plant that can be shaped into dense bushes.
plants.careNotes: Trim into shape regularly.

plants.name: Red Cabomba
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Bright red, finely feathered fanwort; one of the most demanding red plants.
plants.careNotes: Needs very strong light, CO2 and soft water.

legal.note: Do not confuse with Carolina fanwort (Cabomba caroliniana), which has been on the EU Union list since 2016.

plants.name: Hornwort
plants.substrate: Rootless – floating or loosely anchored in the substrate
plants.description: Rootless, very fast-growing plant; strong nutrient competitor against algae, also suitable for cold water and goldfish.
plants.careNotes: Sheds needles when conditions change; thin out regularly.

plants.name: Brazilian Waterweed
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Undemanding plant for cold-water and beginner tanks.
plants.careNotes: Grows poorly in warm water above 26 °C.

legal.note: Not on the EU Union list, but invasive outside its native range. Related species (Elodea nuttallii, Lagarosiphon major) are banned throughout the EU. Never dispose of into natural waters.

plants.name: Water Sprite
plants.substrate: Planted or floating
plants.description: Fast-growing fern with finely divided leaves; can also be used as a floating plant.
plants.careNotes: Forms many plantlets on the leaf edges.

plants.name: Brazilian Pennywort
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Plant with round leaves that grows to the surface and floats there.
plants.careNotes: Trim shoots regularly.

legal.note: Do not confuse with Hydrocotyle ranunculoides (EU Union list).

plants.name: Amazon Frogbit
plants.substrate: Floating, no substrate
plants.description: Floating plant with roundish, spongy leaves and long roots; shelter for labyrinth fish and fry.
plants.careNotes: Takes CO2 from the air. Blocks light when growing strongly – thin out regularly.

plants.name: Red Root Floater
plants.substrate: Floating, no substrate
plants.description: Small floating plant that turns red in strong light and forms red roots.
plants.careNotes: Sensitive to condensation and strong surface movement.

plants.name: Common Duckweed
plants.substrate: Floating, no substrate
plants.description: Tiny floating plant that multiplies explosively; strong nutrient competitor.
plants.careNotes: Hard to remove completely – use deliberately. Eaten by goldfish.

plants.name: Anubias nana 'Petite'
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Very small cultivar ('Bonsai') with leaves only a few centimetres in size; ideal for nano tanks and details on stones.
plants.careNotes: Like all Anubias slow-growing and prone to algae on old leaves.

plants.name: Anubias 'Coffeefolia'
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Anubias with wavy leaves reminiscent of coffee leaves and reddish new growth.
plants.careNotes: Do not bury the rhizome.

plants.name: Java Fern 'Windeløv'
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Java fern form with finely laciniated leaf tips.
plants.careNotes: Attach to wood or stone like Java fern.

plants.name: Narrow Leaf Java Fern
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Java fern with very narrow leaves; looks more delicate than the normal form.
plants.careNotes: Hardy and undemanding.

plants.name: Java Fern 'Trident'
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Java fern with three- to five-lobed, narrow leaves.
plants.careNotes: Hardy; good structural plant on roots.

plants.name: Hygrophila pinnatifida
plants.substrate: Planted or on wood/stone (forms clinging side shoots)
plants.description: Plant with brown-patched, pinnatifid leaves and a burgundy underside; the side shoots cling to wood and stone.
plants.careNotes: Pinch the top shoots for compact growth; plenty of light ensures dense plants.

plants.name: Weeping Moss
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Moss with drooping, overhanging shoots; attractive on roots and stone edges.
plants.careNotes: Attach to raised structures so it can hang down.

plants.name: Flame Moss
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Moss with upright, twisted, flame-like shoots.
plants.careNotes: Grows upwards – good for vertical accents.

plants.name: Taiwan Moss
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Moss similar to Java moss, but more evenly and finely branched.
plants.careNotes: Thin out regularly.

plants.name: Stringy Moss
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Fine, thread-like moss that streams in the current.
plants.careNotes: Also grows at cool temperatures.

plants.name: Mini Pellia
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Very fine, branched liverwort for small details on stones.
plants.careNotes: Prefers rather cooler water and good water quality.

plants.name: Willow Moss
plants.substrate: Epiphyte – tie or glue to wood or stone, do not bury the rhizome
plants.description: Large native European water moss for cold-water and garden pond tanks.
plants.careNotes: Does not tolerate permanent temperatures above 24 °C well.

legal.note: Native European species – buy only from the trade, do not collect from the wild; never introduce into other waters.

plants.name: Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Brown'
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Brown form of Wendt's water trumpet.
plants.careNotes: Avoid replanting if possible (crypt melt).

plants.name: Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Tropica'
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Variety with dark, hammered leaves; according to Tropica it grows well in hard water like most Sri Lankan Cryptocorynes.
plants.careNotes: In open spaces the leaves lie almost on the ground.

plants.name: Cryptocoryne lutea 'Hobbit'
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Very small Cryptocoryne cultivar from Dennerle for the foreground.
plants.careNotes: No CO2 required.

plants.name: Cryptocoryne affinis
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Cryptocoryne with dark green, wavy leaves and a reddish underside.
plants.careNotes: Spreads via runners into dense stands.

plants.name: Cryptocoryne pontederiifolia
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Light green Cryptocoryne with heart-shaped leaves.
plants.careNotes: Slow but hardy.

plants.name: Cryptocoryne x willisii
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Small, narrow-leaved Cryptocoryne for the foreground.
plants.careNotes: Slowly forms low groups.

plants.name: Cryptocoryne spiralis
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Cryptocoryne with long, narrow leaves for the background.
plants.careNotes: Hardy, also in harder water.

plants.name: Cryptocoryne 'Flamingo'
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Pink cultivar – one of the few pink aquarium plants.
plants.careNotes: Colours more intensely with more light.

plants.name: Lagenandra 'Red'
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Plant related to Cryptocorynes with pink-red to red-brown leaves.
plants.careNotes: Slow and hardy; usually left alone by herbivores.

plants.name: Blyxa japonica
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Grass-like plant from nutrient-rich shallow waters, made famous by Takashi Amano's aquascapes.
plants.careNotes: Reddish leaf tips in good light.

plants.name: Echinodorus 'Rubin'
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Large, red-brown sword plant; solitary plant for larger tanks.
plants.careNotes: Root fertilisation enhances the colour.

plants.name: Echinodorus 'Red Diamond'
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Compact red sword plant for medium-sized tanks.
plants.careNotes: Deeper red with more light.

plants.name: Radican Sword
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Large sword plant with heart-shaped leaves; easily forms floating and aerial leaves.
plants.careNotes: Remove aerial leaves so the plant stays submerged.

plants.name: Echinodorus 'Vesuvius'
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Sword plant with narrow, spirally twisted leaves.
plants.careNotes: Good light maintains the spiral form.

plants.name: Dwarf Sword 'Quadricostatus'
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Narrow-leaved dwarf sword that quickly forms a dense lawn.
plants.careNotes: Spreads strongly via runners.

plants.name: Echinodorus argentinensis
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Large sword plant with broad, sturdy leaves.
plants.careNotes: Also tolerates somewhat cooler temperatures.

plants.name: Echinodorus 'Kleiner Bär'
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Compact cultivar with red-brown tinged leaves.
plants.careNotes: Root fertilisation enhances the colour.

plants.name: Straight Vallisneria
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Classic green Vallisneria; quickly forms dense background stands.
plants.careNotes: Remove runners regularly.

plants.name: Dwarf Vallisneria
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Narrow-leaved Vallisneria; finer than the common species.
plants.careNotes: Good for medium-height tanks.

plants.name: Corkscrew Vallisneria
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Vallisneria with corkscrew-twisted leaves.
plants.careNotes: Stays lower than the normal form.

plants.name: Umbrella Hairgrass
plants.propagation: Adventitious plantlets at the stem tips
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Tall, fine hairgrass that forms new plantlets at the stem tips; looks like delicate trees ('bonsai look').
plants.careNotes: Let stems float or trim to length.

plants.name: Creeping Rush
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Grass-like rush that turns reddish in strong light.
plants.careNotes: Trimming promotes bushy growth.

plants.name: Cyperus helferi
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: One of the few truly submersed sedges; fine, flowing stems.
plants.careNotes: Grows slowly; divide the clumps.

plants.name: Aponogeton ulvaceus
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Large Aponogeton with translucent, wavy leaves; forms spreading solitary plants.
plants.careNotes: Enters dormancy; do not remove the tuber then.

plants.name: Aponogeton boivinianus
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Aponogeton with dark green, strongly puckered leaves.
plants.careNotes: Needs regular dormancy periods.

plants.name: Madagascar Lace Plant
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Famous lace plant with lattice-like perforated leaves; demanding.
plants.careNotes: Needs soft, clean, rather cool water and dormancy periods; avoid algae on the lace leaves.

plants.name: Aponogeton undulatus
plants.propagation: Adventitious plantlets on the flower stalk
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Aponogeton with wavy leaves that forms plantlets instead of flowers.
plants.careNotes: No pronounced dormancy.

plants.name: Orchid Lily (Barclaya)
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Water lily relative with long, wavy, often reddish leaves.
plants.careNotes: Prefers warm, soft water.

plants.name: Thai Onion Plant
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Bulb plant with very long, ribbon-like leaves that float at the surface.
plants.careNotes: Only for tall tanks; resistant to herbivores.

plants.name: Nymphoides hydrophylla 'Taiwan'
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Floating heart with water-lily-like green leaves; stays compact when trimmed.
plants.careNotes: Remove floating leaves.

plants.name: Micranthemum umbrosum
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Small-leaved pearlweed with round leaves; creeping or bushy.
plants.careNotes: Trim regularly.

plants.name: Bladderwort (Utricularia graminifolia)
plants.substrate: Fine, nutrient-poor substrate; no true roots
plants.description: Carnivorous plant with bladder traps that forms a grass-like lawn; according to Tropica an ideal but rather demanding carpeting plant.
plants.careNotes: Lives in nutrient-poor habitats in nature; sensitive to disturbance.

plants.name: Whorled Pennywort
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Pennywort with round, umbrella-like stalked leaves.
plants.careNotes: Spreads quickly.

legal.note: Do not confuse with Hydrocotyle ranunculoides (EU Union list).

plants.name: Lindernia rotundifolia
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Undemanding stem plant with small, round leaves.
plants.careNotes: The variegated form 'Variegata' is also common.

plants.name: Bacopa australis
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Small-leaved Bacopa that grows creeping in good light.
plants.careNotes: Upright in low light.

plants.name: Ranunculus inundatus
plants.substrate: Root feeder – nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
plants.description: Carpeting plant with finely divided, 'celery-like' leaves.
plants.careNotes: Prefers rather cooler water.

plants.name: Lobelia cardinalis 'Mini'
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Compact mutation of the cardinal flower with densely set, light green leaves; branches even without trimming.
plants.careNotes: Most compact with good light and CO2, but according to Tropica also thrives without.

plants.name: Rotala 'Green'
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Light green, fine-leaved Rotala that can easily be shaped into bushes.
plants.careNotes: Creeping growth in strong light.

plants.name: Rotala 'H'ra'
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Narrow-leaved Rotala with overhanging to creeping growth; with strong light, CO2 and fertiliser almost exclusively creeping and rich orange.
plants.careNotes: Can be trimmed into an orange cushion or carpet.

plants.name: Giant Red Rotala
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Magnificent deep red Rotala; according to Tropica very demanding – plenty of light, CO2 and soft water are decisive.
plants.careNotes: Do not plant shoots too close together, otherwise the lower leaves get no light; sufficient micronutrients for good colour.

plants.name: Rotala 'Bonsai'
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Compact, slow-growing Rotala with small, whorled leaves.
plants.careNotes: Good for the foreground and nano tanks.

plants.name: Needle Leaf Ludwigia
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Ludwigia with narrow, needle-shaped, copper-red leaves.
plants.careNotes: Red only in good light.

plants.name: Ludwigia 'Pantanal'
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Magnificent red Ludwigia with whorled leaves; one of the most demanding stem plants.
plants.careNotes: Needs soft water, plenty of light, CO2 and good nutrient supply.

plants.name: Limnophila aromatica
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Stem plant with purple-reddish shoot tips and an aromatic scent.
plants.careNotes: Colour depends strongly on light.

plants.name: Limnophila hippuridoides
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Stem plant with whorled leaves and purple colouration.
plants.careNotes: Dark purple in good light.

plants.name: Hygrophila 'Rosanervig'
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Cultivar with pink-veined leaves.
plants.careNotes: As vigorous as the green form.

legal.note: Like Hygrophila polysperma: classified as invasive in the USA – never let it get into natural waters.

plants.name: Hygrophila 'Siamensis 53B'
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: More compact, narrow-leaved form of Giant Hygrophila.
plants.careNotes: Grows more slowly than the normal form.

plants.name: Hygrophila 'Araguaia'
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Small Hygrophila with narrow, reddish leaves.
plants.careNotes: Compact and red in strong light.

plants.name: Red Milfoil
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Finely feathered, red milfoil.
plants.careNotes: Needs plenty of light, CO2 and iron; sensitive to debris.

legal.note: Do not confuse with Myriophyllum aquaticum and M. heterophyllum (EU Union list).

plants.name: Water Hedge
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Fine stem plant with needle-shaped leaves that turns reddish in strong light.
plants.careNotes: Sensitive to nutrient deficiency.

plants.name: Golden Creeping Jenny
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Yellow-green form of the native European creeping jenny; suitable for cold-water and temperate tanks.
plants.careNotes: Grows slowly submersed; permanently above 26 °C is unfavourable.

plants.name: Bacopa salzmannii
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Bacopa with purple shoot tips in good light.
plants.careNotes: Turns purple in strong light.

plants.name: Stream Bogmoss
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Light green stem plant with moss-like fine leaves.
plants.careNotes: Needs soft, iron-rich water.

plants.name: Cardinal Flower
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Stem plant with light green underwater leaves; according to Tropica popular in the 'plant streets' of Dutch aquariums.
plants.careNotes: Forms scarlet flowers above water; also suitable for garden ponds.

plants.name: Canadian Waterweed
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Undemanding cold-water plant for goldfish and pond tanks.
plants.careNotes: Grows poorly in tropically warm water.

legal.note: Not on the EU Union list, but naturalised in Europe; the related Nuttall's waterweed (E. nuttallii) is banned. Never dispose of into natural waters.

plants.name: Yellow Cabomba
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Finely feathered, light green fanwort with yellow floating flowers.
plants.careNotes: Needs plenty of light and soft water.

legal.note: Do not confuse with Carolina fanwort (Cabomba caroliniana, EU Union list).

plants.name: Pogostemon erectus
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Stem plant with needle-shaped, whorled leaves; looks like fine fir trees.
plants.careNotes: Good light for compact growth.

plants.name: Pogostemon 'Octopus'
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Stem plant with long, narrow leaves that wave in the current like octopus arms.
plants.careNotes: Grows fast; trim regularly.

plants.name: Mermaid Weed
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Stem plant with comb-like divided, orange-red leaves.
plants.careNotes: Colour only in strong light.

plants.name: Alternanthera reineckii 'Cardinalis'
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Broad-leaved, intensely red form of Alternanthera.
plants.careNotes: Good light and iron for red colouration.

plants.name: Ammannia 'Golden'
plants.substrate: Insert into the substrate; takes nutrients mainly from the water
plants.description: Yellow-orange stem plant for colour accents.
plants.careNotes: Demanding; needs plenty of light and nutrients.

plants.name: Giant Duckweed
plants.substrate: Floating, no substrate
plants.description: Larger relative of duckweed with a red leaf underside.
plants.careNotes: Multiplies strongly; use deliberately.

legal.note: Native European species – buy only from the trade, do not collect from the wild; never introduce into other waters.

plants.name: Purple-fringed Riccia
plants.substrate: Floating, no substrate
plants.description: Heart-shaped, floating liverwort rosettes with a purple underside.
plants.careNotes: Sensitive to condensation and strong surface movement.

legal.note: Native European species – buy only from the trade, do not collect from the wild; never introduce into other waters.

plants.name: European Frogbit
plants.substrate: Floating, no substrate
plants.description: Native European floating plant with water-lily-like leaves for cold-water and pond tanks.
plants.careNotes: Forms winter buds in autumn; not permanent in tropical tanks.

legal.note: Native European species – buy only from the trade, do not collect from the wild; never introduce into other waters.

plants.name: Chaetomorpha (Spaghetti Algae)
plants.description: Thread-like green alga that grows as a loose, floating mass and does not attach to rock; considered the most stable macroalga for nutrient export in the refugium.
plants.careNotes: Thin out the mass regularly so light reaches the inside; tumble it gently with water flow.

plants.name: Caulerpa prolifera
plants.description: Green alga with leaf-like fronds that spreads via runners in the sand; effective for nutrient export.
plants.careNotes: Can reproduce sexually ('going sexual'): it then turns white, dissolves and releases nutrients and cell material into the water. Prune regularly; keep away from corals.

plants.name: Grape Caulerpa
plants.description: Green alga with grape-like vesicles; readily eaten by surgeonfish.
plants.careNotes: According to TFH the species most likely to go sexual in the aquarium – keep only in the refugium and in limited amounts.

plants.name: Money Plant (Halimeda)
plants.description: Calcareous green alga made of coin-shaped segments; grows on rock or in sand.
plants.careNotes: Consumes calcium and carbonate – keep values in the reef range.

plants.name: Gracilaria (Ogo)
plants.description: Branched red alga used as fresh food for herbivorous fish such as surgeonfish.
plants.careNotes: Plenty of light and flow; surgeonfish quickly eat it in the display tank.

plants.name: Sea Lettuce
plants.description: Leaf-like green alga; nutrient export and food for herbivorous fish.
plants.careNotes: Needs plenty of light and flow.

plants.name: Turtle Grass
plants.description: True seagrass with ribbon-like leaves for lagoon tanks.
plants.careNotes: Needs a deep, fine sand bed for the roots and plenty of light; sensitive to transplanting.

plants.name: Red Mangrove
plants.description: Tree whose roots stand in seawater and whose leaves grow above the surface; mainly decorative.
plants.careNotes: Grows far too slowly for significant nutrient export; mist leaves regularly with fresh water (salt crusts).

plants.name: Serrated Caulerpa
plants.description: Caulerpa with twisted, serrated fronds; grows more slowly than other species.
plants.careNotes: As with all Caulerpa watch for sexual reproduction and prune regularly.

plants.name: Feather Caulerpa
plants.description: Caulerpa with feather-like fronds; commonly offered in the trade.
plants.careNotes: Can overgrow corals – only in the refugium or under control.

plants.name: Fern Caulerpa
plants.description: Caulerpa with fern-like feathered fronds.
plants.careNotes: Thin out regularly.

plants.name: Red Grape Algae
plants.description: Red alga with red, grape-like vesicles; not related to Caulerpa.
plants.careNotes: Needs strong flow and good light.

plants.name: Shaving Brush Plant
plants.description: Calcareous green alga that looks like a shaving brush and roots in the sand.
plants.careNotes: According to Quality Marine at specific gravity 1.023–1.025, 22–26 °C, pH 8.1–8.4 and 8–12 °dKH.

plants.name: Mermaid's Fan
plants.description: Fan-shaped, calcareous green alga that roots in the sand.
plants.careNotes: Slow-growing; keep calcium and KH stable.

plants.name: Manatee Grass
plants.description: Seagrass with round, thread-like leaves.
plants.careNotes: Needs a deep sand bed and plenty of light.

plants.name: Dark Spleenwort
plants.origin: Africa and Asia; aquarium stock from Taiwan
plants.propagation: Plantlets on the leaves, rhizome division
plants.substrate: Attach to rock or wood; leave the rhizome exposed.
plants.description: Slow-growing aquarium fern; formerly sold under an incorrect Crepidomanes name.
plants.careNotes: Attach to rock or wood; leave the rhizome exposed.
